issues.title: Feature Request: Line-level repetition detection to break thinking loops
issues.body_head:
## Problem

Reasoning/thinking models (Qwen3, DeepSeek-R1, GPT-OSS, GLM-4 and others) frequently get stuck in semantic loops during the thinking phase, repeating the same line or pair of lines indefinitely:

```
We also need to mention that the code uses a return statement at the end to return true.
We also need to mention that the code uses a return statement inside the loop to exit early.
We also need to mention that the code uses a return statement at the end to return true.
We also need to mention that the code uses a return statement inside the loop to exit early.
...
```

This is distinct from token-level repetition that `repeat_penalty` addresses. Each line is internally varied at the token level (different phrasing each time), so token-based penalties don't catch it. The loop only becomes visible at the **line level**.

The result is wasted compute, ballooning context, and in many cases the model never escaping the loop within any reasonable token budget. This has been reported repeatedly: #20353, #18268 and related Ollama issues.

## Proposed Solution

A **line-level repetition sampler** that operates at `\n` boundaries — computationally very cheap since it only runs once per newline token:

1. Maintain a sliding window of the last N generated lines (e.g. N=20, configurable)
2. When a `\n` token is generated, compare the completed line against all lines in the window
3. On match: apply a **temperature boost** for the next K tokens to inject diversity and help the model escape — rather than hard-truncating, which leaves the model mid-thought

This pairs naturally with **Dynamic Temperature** (`dynatemp_range`): dynatemp works preventively based on entropy; line-detection acts as a hard fallback when a loop forms anyway. Together they provide layered loop resistance.

### Parameters (suggested)

| Parameter | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `repeat_line_window` | 0 (disabled) | Number of recent lines to check against |
| `repeat_line_temp_boost` | 0.4 | Temperature added on line match |
| `repeat_line_boost_tokens` | 16 | How many tokens the boost applies for |

## Why Not Existing Mechanisms?

- **`repeat_penalty`**: token-level, misses semantic loops with varied phrasing
- **`--reasoning-budget` / hard truncation** (PR #21141): cuts the thinking block but doesn't help the model escape — it just stops it
- **`dynatemp_range`**: entropy-based, preventive — but once the model is confident about a looping phrase, entropy is low and dynatemp al

The server appears to re-parse the entire model response turn for every single token generated, and the model continuously repeats the same tool call without ever reaching an EOT (End of Turn) or EOS.

Actual Behavior

The model generates a tool call, but instead of finishing the turn, it repeats the same call indefinitely. The logs show the PEG parser running a full re-parse for every token:

The server continues to send streamed chunks for the same tool call index (e.g., index: 83) repeatedly. The model never exits the <|tool_call|> block.

issues.title: Per-head adaptive KV cache quantization: lossless q4_0 on hybrid models, +8% quality on standard models
issues.body_head:
## Summary

Two findings from production benchmarks of `-ctk q4_0 -ctv q4_0`:

1. **q4_0 KV cache is completely lossless on hybrid models** (Qwen3.5) -- BLEU 1.000 across 10 test configurations at 4x compression
2. **For standard models** (Llama, Mistral), per-head entropy-adaptive bit allocation improves quality by +8% BLEU at the same compression ratio

Feature request: per-head KV cache type support to enable adaptive allocation.

## Finding 1: Lossless q4_0 on Hybrid Models

A/B benchmarks on RTX 3060 12GB, Qwen3.5-9B, 3-run averages:

| Test | f16 gen/s | q4_0 gen/s | Speed Diff |
|------|-----------|------------|------------|
| Short (2-turn) | 48.2 | 47.0 | -2.4% |
| Medium (8-turn) | 47.0 | 45.8 | -2.6% |
| Long (20+ turn) | 45.9 | 45.8 | -0.1% |

Quality: **BLEU 1.000** (n=50 completions). Token-level identical output between f16 and q4_0 KV cache.

The 33K-token conversation test ran at 36.5 tok/s on q4_0 -- f16 would OOM on the same 12GB GPU.

## Why Hybrid Models Tolerate q4_0

Qwen3.5 uses only **8 of 32 layers** for full attention with KV cache. The other 24 layers use linear attention (Gated Delta Net) with no KV cache. Similarly, Gemma 4 uses **10 of 60 layers** for global attention.

The linear/sliding attention layers act as error correction -- quantization noise in the few attention layers is absorbed by the surrounding layers. Standard models (Llama, Mistral) have no such correction because all layers use full attention.

## Finding 2: Entropy-Adaptive Allocation for Standard Models

For standard architectures where q4_0 does degrade quality, per-head bit allocation based on attention entropy recovers most of the loss:

```
b_h = b_avg + 0.25 * (H_avg - H_2(h))
```

Where `H_2(h)` is the Renyi entropy of head h's attention distribution.

Results on GPT-2 (all at 4x compression):

| Config | BLEU | Token Match | PPL Ratio |
|--------|------|-------------|-----------|
| Uniform 4-bit | 0.531 | 51.3% | 1.101 |
| Adaptive 4-bit | 0.548 | 53.8% | 1.089 |
| Skip 3 sinks + adaptive | 0.574 | 60.0% | 1.062 |

The key insight: the bottom 2% of heads by entropy ("sink heads") contribute disproportionately to quantization error. Skipping quantization on just 3 out of 144 heads provides more benefit than optimal bit redistribution across all others.

## Feature Request: Per-Head KV Cache Types

Currently `-ctk` and `-ctv` apply uniformly to all layers and heads. Per-head allocation would enable:

- **Sink heads** (lowest entropy, ~2% of heads): kee

issues.title: Eval bug: Gemma 4 fails to load with tensor shape mismatch due to sliding_window_pattern read as uint32_t instead of bool
issues.body_head:
### Name and Version

version: b8661 (b7ad48e)
built with MSVC 19.44.35211.0 for Windows x86_64
CMake options: GGML_CUDA=ON, GGML_CUDA_FA=ON, GGML_CUDA_GRAPHS=ON, BUILD_SHARED_LIBS=ON, LLAMA_OPENSSL=ON
CUDA 12.9

### Operating systems

Windows

### GGML backends

CUDA

### Hardware

AMD Ryzen 7 7800X3D + NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4070 (12GB VRAM)

### Models

unsloth/gemma-4-26B-A4B-it-GGUF (UD-Q4_K_M)
https://huggingface.co/unsloth/gemma-4-26B-A4B-it-GGUF

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

## Summary
Attempting to load a Gemma 4 model (e.g., `gemma-4-26B-A4B-it-GGUF`) with a self-compiled build from source fails with a tensor shape mismatch error:
```
llama_model_load: error loading model: check_tensor_dims: tensor 'blk.1.attn_q.weight' has wrong shape; expected 2816, 8192, got 2816, 4096
```
However, the same model loads and works correctly in LM Studio v2.11.0, which uses a forked version of llama.cpp.

## Root Cause
The GGUF file stores `gemma4.attention.sliding_window_pattern` as a `bool[]` array (30 entries). The llama.cpp loader reads this into `std::array<uint32_t, LLAMA_MAX_LAYERS> swa_layers` via `get_key_or_arr`. Due to the type mismatch between `bool` (1 byte) and `uint32_t` (4 bytes), the memory layout is misinterpreted, causing incorrect `is_swa()` results for most layers. This leads to wrong dimension calculations for `n_embd_head_k` and `n_embd_k_gqa`, resulting in the tensor shape mismatch.

## Fix
Changing `swa_layers` from `std::array<uint32_t, LLAMA_MAX_LAYERS>` to `std::array<bool, LLAMA_MAX_LAYERS>` and adding the necessary `get_arr<bool, 512>` template instantiation resolves the issue completely. The model then loads correctly, producing the same `n_embd_k_gqa` values as LM Studio.

### First Bad Commit

_No response_

### Relevant log output

## Error log (before fix)
```console
$ llama-server -m gemma-4-26B-A4B-it-UD-Q4_K_M.gguf --ctx-size 8192 --n-gpu-layers 30 --flash-attn on --cpu-moe
print_info: arch                  = gemma4
print_info: n_embd_k_gqa          = [2048, 4096, 2048, 2048, 2048, 512, 2048, 4096, ...]
print_info: n_embd_v_gqa          = [2048, 4096, 2048, 2048, 2048, 512, 2048, 4096, ...]
load_tensors: loading model tensors, this can take a while... (mmap = true, direct_io = false)
llama_model_load: error loading model: check_tensor_dims: tensor 'blk.1.attn_q.weight' has wrong shape; expected 2816, 8192, got 2816, 4096
```

## Expected output (after fix)
```console

issues.title: Eval bug: F16 KV cache accuracy degrades when --ctx-size < model native context
issues.body_head:
### Name and Version

EULLM Engine v0.3.6 (llama-cpp-2 Rust crate 0.1.141, llama.cpp backend: AmesianX/TurboQuant v1.4.2 — base commit f5d1c4179)


### Operating systems

Linux

### GGML backends

CUDA

### Hardware

AMD Ryzen 9 5950X 16-Core Processor + RTX5070TI 16GB

### Models

qwen3-14b.gguf

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

F16 KV cache produces degraded accuracy when `--ctx-size` is set below the model's native context length, even though F16 is lossless and the actual prompt length is well within both windows.

Tested with Qwen3-14B-Q4_K_M (native context: 32768 tokens).

Steps to reproduce:

1. Start server with ctx-size BELOW native context:
   ./llama-server -m qwen3-14b-q4_k_m.gguf \
     --cache-type-k f16 --cache-type-v f16 \
     --ctx-size 16384

2. Run math recall benchmark with filler distances 200–2500 tokens
   (91 problems: 2×2 matrix mul, 3×3 matrix mul, scalar arithmetic chains)
   --no-think to disable Qwen3 extended reasoning

3. Repeat with --ctx-size 32768 (native), identical prompts

Results:
  ctx-size 16384 → 75/91 (82.4%) — collapses to 27.8% above 1500t actual context
  ctx-size 32768 → 91/91 (100%) — perfect across all distances including 2500t filler (ctx~1780t)

Key observation: actual prompt at 2500t filler is only ~1780 tokens — well within BOTH
context windows. F16 is lossless so KV cache corruption is not possible. The degradation
must come from the attention computation itself (hypothesis: RoPE frequency scaling
applied when ctx-size < model native context distorts positional encodings at longer distances).

Reproduced with EULLM Engine v0.3.6 (llama-cpp-2 Rust crate 0.1.141,
AmesianX/TurboQuant v1.4.2 fork, base commit f5d1c4179) and independently
verified on upstream llama-server.
Benchmark script: https://github.com/eullm/eullm/blob/main/bench/turboquant_math_accuracy.py



### First Bad Commit

Unknown — not bisected. Present in llama-cpp-2 0.1.141 / llama.cpp f5d1c4179.


### Relevant log output

Accuracy by context size (prompt tokens) — ctx-size 16384:

  Range        Pass/Total    %       Avg ctx
  0–500  t     38/39        97.4%   228t
  500–1000 t   12/13        92.3%   785t
  1000–1500 t  20/21        95.2%   1265t
  1500–2000 t   5/18        27.8%   1738t   ← collapse

Accuracy by context size (prompt tokens) — ctx-size 32768 (same prompts):

  Range        Pass/Total    %       Avg ctx

issues.title: Finding: asymmetric K/V quantization (3b-K/2b-V) gives 6x better quality than symmetric — architecture dependent
issues.body_head:
Hey folks,

Sharing some KV cache compression results that might be relevant for llama.cpp's quantized KV cache work.

We've been developing NexusQuant, which uses E8 lattice vector quantization for KV cache compression. A few findings that might be useful:

**Asymmetric K/V matters a lot:** 3-bit keys + 2-bit values gives 6x better quality than symmetric 2-bit on Mistral-7B. This is consistent with what the TurboQuant+ folks found on llama.cpp. Keys are more sensitive because quantization noise propagates through softmax across all positions. Values are linearly combined, so their noise stays proportional.

**Architecture-dependent behavior:** Qwen2.5-7B completely breaks with any symmetric KV quantization (PPL goes astronomical). Protecting the first/last 2 layers at FP16 recovers it. Mistral and Phi-3 are fine without this. Worth checking if llama.cpp's KV quant has similar model-dependent behavior.

**K4V2 diminishing returns:** Going from 3-bit to 4-bit keys barely helps (+0.06pp). The softmax error floor is reached around 3-bit. This suggests the current Q4_0/Q5_0 KV quant in llama.cpp might be allocating more bits to keys than needed.

Our approach is Python-based (not useful for llama.cpp directly), but the findings about asymmetric bit allocation and boundary layer sensitivity might inform llama.cpp's KV quantization strategy.

Results + paper: https://github.com/jagmarques/nexusquant

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

First reported here:  https://github.com/lemonade-sdk/llamacpp-rocm/issues/75


On multi-GPU systems, the CUDA/HIP backend calls `cudaMemcpyPeerAsync()` to share data between devices. If the system does not support peer device memory access, the data gets corrupted.

The work-around is to build with `-DGGML_CUDA_NO_PEER_COPY=ON`.

The fix would be to call `cudaMemcpyPeerAsync()` only if peer device memory access is supported (can be queried with `cudaDeviceCanAccessPeer()`).

There is a check in this function, but it doesn't seem to do anything if peer device memory access is not supported: https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/d12cc3d1ca6bba741cd77887ac9c9ee18c8415c7/ggml/src/ggml-cuda/ggml-cuda.cu#L1428

issues.title: BPE tokenizer: incorrect Cyrillic tokenization for MiniMax-M2
issues.body_head:
[minimax-m2-cyrillic-fix.patch](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/26603790/minimax-m2-cyrillic-fix.patch)

# GitHub Issue: BPE tokenizer incorrect Cyrillic tokenization for MiniMax-M2

## Title
BPE tokenizer: incorrect Cyrillic tokenization for MiniMax-M2 (lowercase→uppercase boundary not detected)

## Labels
bug, tokenizer

---

## Bug Description

The BPE pre-tokenizer regex for `LLAMA_VOCAB_PRE_TYPE_MINIMAX_M2` (and `GPT4O`) uses `[^a-z]`/`[^A-Z]` to detect letter case boundaries, which only works for Latin characters. This causes incorrect tokenization of Cyrillic (and likely other non-Latin scripts).

## Why This Is Critical

This bug is a **blocker for using llama.cpp with 1C:Enterprise (1С:Предприятие)** — a major ERP platform widely used in Russia and CIS countries. 

In 1C, metadata object names follow CamelCase convention in Cyrillic, e.g.:
- `ДокументПродажиТоваровУслуг` (SalesDocument)
- `СправочникКонтрагентовОрганизации` (ContractorsDirectory)
- `РегистрНакопленияОстаткиТоваров` (InventoryAccumulationRegister)

When using LLMs as coding agents for 1C development, the model must correctly reproduce these identifiers in tool calls and generated code. This tokenization bug causes the model to corrupt object names after the first usage, making AI-assisted 1C development impossible with affected models.

## Steps to Reproduce

```bash
./build/bin/llama-tokenize -m /path/to/MiniMax-M2.5.gguf -p "ПримерДлинногоИмениОбъекта"
```

## Expected Result (matches HuggingFace tokenizer)

```
11579 -> 'ного'
11706 -> 'И'
53535 -> 'мени'
```

## Actual Result (llama.cpp)

```
73904 -> 'ног'
751 -> 'о�'      # broken UTF-8
152 -> '�'       # broken UTF-8
53535 -> 'мени'
```

The uppercase Cyrillic `И` is incorrectly split into raw UTF-8 bytes (tokens 751 and 152), causing generation issues. When the model tries to reproduce this string, it outputs garbage like `defendant`, `被告`, or other random tokens.

## Root Cause

In `llama-vocab.cpp` line ~432, the adapted regex uses:

```cpp
"[^\\r\\n\\p{L}\\p{N}]?((?=[\\p{L}])([^a-z]))*((?=[\\p{L}])([^A-Z]))+..."
```

The patterns `[^a-z]` and `[^A-Z]` only match **Latin** letters. Cyrillic letters like `О`, `А`, `И` are not in `a-z`/`A-Z` ranges, so the pre-tokenizer doesn't detect the lowercase→uppercase boundary at `ного` → `Имени`.

The original regex from MiniMax's `tokenizer.json` uses proper Unicode properties:

```
[\p{Lu}\p{Lt}\p{Lm}\p{Lo}\p{M}]*[\p{Ll}\p{Lm}\p{Lo}\p{M}]+
```

issues.title: Misc. bug: dual-GPU inference produces gibberish on asymmetric PCIe topology, while single-GPU works and older build b7728 works correctly
issues.body_head:
### NOTE about related issue

I am aware of issue #20052. I do not cite it as proof of a llama.cpp bug, only as a similar symptom on a comparable asymmetric non-P2P topology. In that case, the final conclusion was hardware-induced corruption via a marginal riser cable, not a llama.cpp software defect.

### Summary

I am seeing a regression in dual-GPU inference on llama.cpp.

On the same machine, with the same GPUs, same model, and same physical topology:

- older build `b7728` works correctly on 2 GPUs
- newer build `b8783-e21cdc11a` produces gibberish or hangs/stalls during generation on 2 GPUs
- single-GPU works on both builds

This looks like a regression in the multi-GPU execution path between `b7728` and `b8783`.

### Hardware

- Host OS: Debian Linux
- GPUs:
  - 2 x NVIDIA RTX 4000 SFF Ada Generation
  - compute capability 8.9
  - 20 GB VRAM each
- Driver:
  - NVIDIA driver 595.58.03
- PCIe topology:
  - GPU0 in motherboard x16 slot
  - GPU1 connected through a riser in an x4 slot

Important detail: this asymmetric topology is not inherently broken, because `b7728` works correctly on 2 GPUs on the exact same machine and same setup.

### Model

- `ggml-org/gpt-oss-20b-GGUF`
- file: `gpt-oss-20b-mxfp4.gguf`

### What works

#### 1) Old build, single GPU

`b7728` works correctly on 1 GPU.

Observed generation speed:

- about 85 tok/s

#### 2) Old build, dual GPU

`b7728` also works correctly on 2 GPUs on the same machine.

Observed generation speed:

- about 85 tok/s

This means:

- model is fine
- hardware is fine
- the x16 + x4/riser topology is usable
- dual-GPU execution is possible on this system

### What breaks

#### 3) Newer build, single GPU

`b8783-e21cdc11a` works correctly on 1 GPU.

Observed generation speed:

- about 83 tok/s

#### 4) Newer build, dual GPU

`b8783-e21cdc11a` breaks on 2 GPUs.

Symptoms:

- sometimes gibberish output
- sometimes generation does not progress properly
- plain `/completion` endpoint can return garbage even with a tiny deterministic prompt

Example request:

```bash
curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8000/completion \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data-raw '{"prompt":"Reply with exactly one word: hello","n_predict":8,"temperature":0}'

Example bad response on `b8783` dual-GPU:

```json
{"index":0,"content":"vb.t ĐpanHTHTn", ...}
```

Expected output should be something like:

```text
hello
```

### Why this looks like a regression

On the same hardware and same model:

- `b7728` dual-GPU works correctl

issues.title: Misc. bug:  Incorrect usage of __riscv_v_intrinsic macro - should use __riscv_v for RVV separation
issues.body_head:
### Name and Version

version: 8683 (d0a6dfeb2)
built with Clang 20.9.0 for Linux riscv64

### Operating systems

Linux

### Which llama.cpp modules do you know to be affected?

llama-cli

### Command line

```shell

```

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

**Summary**
The llama.cpp codebase incorrectly uses `__riscv_v_intrinsic` for conditional compilation to separate RISC-V Vector (RVV) implementation from scalar code. According to the official RISC-V "V" Vector Extension Intrinsic specification, `__riscv_v` should be used instead.

**The Issue**
According to the [RISC-V "V" Vector Extension Intrinsic Document](https://github.com/riscv-non-isa/riscv-rvv-intrinsic-doc/blob/main/doc/rvv-intrinsic-spec.adoc), section on predefined macros:
**`__riscv_v_intrinsic`**: Version number macro for the intrinsic API
**This macro should be defined even if the vector extension is not enabled.**
**`__riscv_v`**: RVV extension detection macro
Only defined when the vector extension is actually enabled. This is the correct macro for RVV/scalar code separation

**Current State in llama.cpp**
The codebase has inconsistent usage:
1. Correct usage (older code):
https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/81df3f7cfaa6f99de14e792b38d5771bf427383e/ggml/src/ggml-cpu/arch/riscv/quants.c#L39
2. Incorrect usage (newer code)
https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/81df3f7cfaa6f99de14e792b38d5771bf427383e/ggml/src/ggml-cpu/arch/riscv/quants.c#L2061

**Impact**
Using `__riscv_v_intrinsic` instead of `__riscv_v` for RVV separation can lead to runtime crashes, vector instructions executed on hardware without vector support.

# Bug: Q8_0 and Q4_0 KV cache produce gibberish on Qwen 3 1.7B with CPU + KleidiAI backend at HEAD

**Repo:** ggml-org/llama.cpp
**HEAD commit reproduced on:** `7f3f843c3` (submodule pin in our Android wrapper)
**Backend:** CPU only (arm64-v8a), KleidiAI int4 dispatch enabled via `GGML_CPU_KLEIDIAI=ON`
**Model:** Qwen 3 1.7B (`Qwen/Qwen3-1.7B`), GGUF re-quantized to `Q4_K_M` (stock community export)
**Device:** Pixel 10a (Tensor G4, Cortex-X4/A720/A520, 8 GB RAM)
**Build flags:** `GGML_NATIVE=OFF`, `GGML_BACKEND_DL=ON`, `GGML_CPU_ALL_VARIANTS=ON`, `LLAMA_BUILD_COMMON=ON`. Variants compiled and packaged: `armv8.0_1`, `armv8.2_1/2`, `armv8.6_1`, `armv9.0_1`, `armv9.2_1/2`.

## Summary

Setting `ctx_params.type_k = ctx_params.type_v = GGML_TYPE_Q4_0` OR `GGML_TYPE_Q8_0` produces broken output during real inference (gibberish unicode tokens or empty responses), regardless of whether `flash_attn_type` is left at default or explicitly set to `LLAMA_FLASH_ATTN_TYPE_ENABLED`. `GGML_TYPE_F16` works correctly.

`llama-bench` does NOT surface the regression — the model loads, prefill and decode both produce plausible tok/s numbers (53 pp, 8 tg), and the bench path itself never exercises the failure mode. Only the full chat-template + tokenizer + sampler path during interactive generation triggers it.

## Reproduction

Three configurations tested on identical code paths (same JNI surface, same chat template, same Hermes 2 Pro tool-call system prompt, same 12-case research-tool fidelity eval):

| `type_k` / `type_v` | `flash_attn_type` | `n_ctx` | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| `F16` (default) | implicit (default) | 4096 | **12/12 pass**, ~5 s per case, sensible output |
| `Q4_0` | `LLAMA_FLASH_ATTN_TYPE_ENABLED` | 4096 | Empty response (`chunks=0`, 88 s wall) |
| `Q8_0` | `LLAMA_FLASH_ATTN_TYPE_ENABLED` | 4096 | Gibberish (`y乎 Ю Öást`, 93 s wall, 7 chunks) |
| `Q8_0` | implicit (default) | 4096 | Gibberish (`éc 況 自ja- ※`, 88 s wall, 7 chunks) |

The bisect on the FA flag isolates the failure to the KV-quant change alone — `flash_attn_type` setting is irrelevant. (llama.cpp auto-enables FA when KV is quantized, so explicit-on and implicit-on resolve to the same path.)

Generation in the failure cases is **also pathologically slow** (0.07–0.08 tok/s vs the 8 tok/s ceiling reported by `llama-bench` on the same context), suggesting a numerical blowup that cascades through the sampler rather than a clean wrong-token output.

llama_context_params ct

**Flags:** --spec-type draft-mtp --spec-draft-n-max 2 --spec-draft-n-min 1 -np 1

## Symptom

Base model (no MTP) runs cleanly at 72.9 tok/s. With --spec-type draft-mtp, first few tokens are correct but output quickly degrades to garbled characters. Draft acceptance drops from 100% (short prompts) to ~2/191 (longer generations).

## Key finding

Same build compiled with Vulkan backend produces clean output at 53 tok/s with 81% draft acceptance — confirming the MTP code is correct. The bug is SYCL-specific.

## Root cause analysis

The MTP head self-prediction step (t_mtp_out hidden state) produces incorrect results on the SYCL backend. The first MTP draft (step k=0, uses main model pre-norm hidden state) is correct. Subsequent drafts (step k>0, use MTP head own predicted hidden state) diverge immediately. Tensor type on SYCL is f32, not a type mismatch.

## What was tried

- --spec-draft-n-max 1 through 5 — all garbled on SYCL
- GGML_SYCL_F16 on/off — no difference
- Vulkan same build: clean output (proves code is correct)

## Working configs

| Config | Tok/s | MTP Acceptance | Output |
|--------|-------|----------------|--------|
| SYCL no MTP | 72.9 | - | Clean |
| SYCL + MTP | 19-31 | ~1% | Garbled |
| Vulkan + MTP | 53.2 | 81% | Clean |

## Environment

- OS: Ubuntu 24.04
- GPU: Intel Arc Pro B70 (32 GB, Battlemage G31)
- oneAPI 2025.3
- IntelLLVM 2025.3.3

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

## Reproduction

### Step 1: Build with Vulkan backend
```bash
cmake -B build -DGGML_VULKAN=ON -DLLAMA_CURL=OFF
cmake --build build --config Release -j $(nproc)
```

### Step 2: Run test-backend-ops
```bash
LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/opt/cixgpu-pro/lib/aarch64-linux-gnu build/bin/test-backend-ops -b Vulkan0 -o MUL_MAT
```

Result: **167 / 860 tests FAIL**.

### Step 3: Observe garbage output in conversation mode
```bash
LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/opt/cixgpu-pro/lib/aarch64-linux-gnu \
  build/bin/llama-cli -m Qwen3-4B-Q4_0.gguf -c 4096 -t 8 --conversation \
  -p "hi, who are you?" -n 64 --no-warmup
```

Output is garbage (repeated `．．．` or completely irrelevant text).

### Step 4: Verify CPU works correctly
```bash
LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/opt/cixgpu-pro/lib/aarch64-linux-gnu \
  build/bin/llama-cli -m Qwen3-4B-Q4_0.gguf -c 4096 -t 8 -ngl 0 --conversation \
  -p "hi, who are you?" -n 64 --no-warmup
```

Output is correct (coherent thinking + response).

## Analysis

### Failure pattern

Failures occur across **all data types** (f32, f16, q4_0, q4_1, q5_0, q8_0, q2_K, q4_K, iq2_xxs, etc.) and **various tensor shapes**. The issue is NOT limited to a specific `n` dimension.

Representative failing cases (sorted by NMSE magnitude):

| NMSE | Shape | Notes |
|------|-------|-------|
| ~2 - 3 | `m=16, n=8/16, k=4, bs=[2,3]` with non-trivial `per` | Moderate error, permutation-related |
| ~22 | `m=64, n=2, k=64, bs=[8,1], nr=[4,1]` | Large batch, small n |
| ~27 | `m=64, n=77, k=77, bs=[12,1]` | Large n, large batch |
| ~97 | `m=16, n=9, k=256` | All types fail here |
| ~115 | `m=16, n=9, k=256, type_a=q4_0` | Q4_0 (common quantization) |
| ~289 | `m=16, n=16, k=1024, bs=[3,2], type_a=mxfp4` | |
| ~321 | `m=16, n=16, k=1024, bs=[3,2], type_a=f32` | |

During the **decode phase** (token-by-token generation), the matmul shape is `n=1, k=hidden_dim`. For this shape the NMSE is ~0.09 — noisy but still correlated with the correct result, so output may look "readable but drifting."

During the **prefill phase** (batch processing the full prompt), the matmul shapes depend on prompt length and model dimensions. Conversation mode ad

### Problem

Gemma4 GGUF tokenization does not match the fixed Hugging Face / Transformers tokenizer behavior.

The HF model folder has been fixed so that Transformers tokenizes the test string correctly:

```python

p = "D:/gemma-4-31B-it"

tok = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(
    p,
    trust_remote_code=True,

issues.title: Eval bug: /v1/embeddings returns HTTP 200 with all-zero embedding vector when served with a causal LM instead of an embedding model (silent incorrect output)
issues.body_head:
### Name and Version

b9272 (1d7ab2b)
built with GNU 11.4.0 for Linux x86_64

### Operating systems

Linux

### GGML backends

CUDA

### Hardware

CUDA0   : NVIDIA H100 80GB HBM3
CPU     : Intel(R) Xeon(R) Gold 6430

### Models

Qwen--Qwen3-4B-GGUF

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

When calling `POST /v1/embeddings` on a `llama_cpp.server` instance loaded with a causal LM (`Qwen3-4B`), the server returns HTTP 200 with a well-formed response, but the embedding vector contains entirely zero values. No error, warning, or log message is produced. The result is silently incorrect.

This is more severe than a crash: the server appears to work correctly, but downstream tasks that rely on the embeddings (semantic search, similarity ranking, clustering, etc.) will produce completely wrong results with no indication that anything went wrong.

## Steps to Reproduce

**Step 1: start the server with a causal LM**
```bash
python -m llama_cpp.server \
  --model <path-to-Qwen3-4B-Q4_K_M.gguf> \
  --host 127.0.0.1 \
  --port 20034
```

**Step 2: send an embedding request**
```bash
curl -s http://127.0.0.1:20034/v1/embeddings \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "model": "Qwen3-4B-Q4_K_M.gguf",
    "input": ["hello world"],
    "encoding_format": "float"
  }'
```

## Expected Behavior

One of the following should happen:

1. The server rejects the embedding request with a clear error explaining that the loaded model is not an embedding model and cannot produce meaningful embeddings, or
2. The server produces a valid, non-zero embedding vector if the model is capable of it.

In either case, returning a silently incorrect all-zero vector with HTTP 200 is not acceptable behavior.

## Actual Behavior

The server returns HTTP 200 with a well-formed response, but the embedding vector is entirely zeros:

```json
{
  "model": "Qwen3-4B-Q4_K_M.gguf",
  "object": "list",
  "usage": {"prompt_tokens": 6, "total_tokens": 6},
  "data": [{
    "embedding": [0.0, 0.0, 0.0, ..., 0.0],
    "index": 0,
    "object": "embedding"
  }]
}
```

The embedding dimension is correct (matching the model's hidden size), but every value is `0.0`. No warning or error is logged by the server.

## Why This Is Dangerous

A zero vector is mathematically degenerate — its cosine similarity to any other vector is undefined or zero, and its dot product with anything is always zero. Any downstream system consuming these embeddings will silently produce wrong results, with no indicatio

issues.title: Eval bug: GLM 5.x crashes/gibberish with high ubatch and long prompts
issues.body_head:
### Name and Version

$ ./build/bin/llama-server --version
version: 9311 (11ee2ddec)
built with IntelLLVM 2026.0.0 for Linux x86_64

But also happens with current clean upstream master

### Operating systems

Linux

### GGML backends

CUDA, CPU, SYCL, Vulkan

### Hardware

- Threadripper, 512GB RAM.
- RTX Pro 6000 WS Blackwell (96GB)
- RTX 3090 (24GB)
- Intel B60 (24GB)

### Models

GLM 5.1

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

This issue has been around for months but I've never managed to track it down.
GLM 5.x (tested 5.1 but should apply to at least 5.0 as well) will crash when fed a very long context cold.
If this context naturally builds up/gets added in pieces, no problem. It only crashes when receiving ~120k+ new tokens in one go.

I have this tracked down and "solved" on my end, but it is AI slop I don't understand and thus in no state for me to PR.

Codex describes the identified cause as:

> GLM 5.1 currently runs through a dense MLA attention path instead of its intended GLM-DSA sparse/indexer attention. On cold very-large prefill, the dense KQ mask scales with KV length * microbatch size and can exceed backend/indexing limits, causing downstream invalid results/crashes; hot long-context generation avoids this because each step has a tiny microbatch.

And its applied workaround:

> Added a GLM-DSA-specific cap on prefill n_ubatch so the dense fallback KQ mask stays below the oversized-mask/backend-indexing danger zone.
> I used a signed 32-bit byte-offset ceiling: keep the dense KQ mask under INT32_MAX bytes, about 2  GiB.
> Since the mask is float, that means roughly: 
> `n_kv * n_ubatch < INT32_MAX / sizeof(float)`
> or about 536M mask elements. 

Which in practice means it dynamically scales down ubatch per batch as needed on long prompts. Comes at a speed penalty by virtue of smaller ubatches but fully prevents the problem for me.


Launch command:
```
./build/bin/llama-server -m /mnt/sda1/models/GLM-5.1-GGUF/GLM-5.1-UD-Q4_K_XL-00001-of-00011.gguf --keep -1 --offline --no-context-shift --flash-attn on --jinja --temp 1 --kv-unified --backend-sampling --parallel 1 --fit off --threads 64 -dev CUDA0,CUDA1,Vulkan1 --tensor-split 1,0,0 --n-gpu-layers 9999 -ot (?:^|\.)blk\.(?:[8-9])\..*ffn_(gate|up|down)_exps\.=CUDA1,(?:^|\.)blk\.(?:1[0-1])\..*ffn_(gate|up|down)_exps\.=Vulkan1,(?:^|\.)blk\.(?:(?:1[2-9]|2[0-9]|3[0-9]|4[0-9]|5[0-9]|6[0-9]|7[0-8]))\..*ffn_(gate|up|down)_exps\.=CPU --batch-size 16384 --ubatch-size 16384 --port 8124
```

issues.title: [OpenCL] ggml_cl_flash_attn: is_causal heuristic incorrectly applies causal masking to ViT full attention, causing completely wrong vision output
issues.body_head:
## Environment

- **Device**: OnePlus Ace 5 (Snapdragon 8 Gen 3, Adreno 750, Android 15)
- **llama.cpp commit**: `35c9b1f39`
- **Model**: Qwen2.5-VL-3B-Instruct (Q4_0 LLM + F16 mmproj)
- **Backend**: OpenCL (`--mmproj-offload -ngl 99`)

## Bug

Running Qwen2.5-VL with the OpenCL backend, the mmproj (ViT visual encoder) produces **completely wrong** visual tokens regardless of the input image. The CPU path is correct; the OpenCL path is functionally broken.

Given a Termux terminal screenshot containing `pkg install` / `pkg search` commands:

| Path | Output | `pkg` token probability |
|---|---|---|
| CPU mmproj (`--no-mmproj-offload`) | correctly identifies `pkg search <query>`, `pkg install <package>` | **89.3%** |
| OpenCL mmproj (`--mmproj-offload`) | hallucinates a Windows file path `C:\Users\...\Main.java` | **6.9%** |

This is not a precision issue — it is a functional failure. The model cannot see the image at all.

## Root Cause

`ggml-opencl.cpp` is the **general-purpose OpenCL GPU backend** for GGML, shared by both LLM and ViT computations. Both call the same `ggml_cl_flash_attn()` function.

The bug is at **line 10889** of `ggml-opencl.cpp`, inside `ggml_cl_flash_attn()`:

```c
const int is_causal = (mask == NULL && n_q > 1 && n_q == n_kv);
```

This heuristic tries to detect LLM causal self-attention by shape alone, but it **incorrectly fires for ViT full-attention layers**:

- ViT full-attention passes `kq_mask = nullptr` — no explicit mask is needed for bidirectional attention
- ViT has `n_q == n_kv == n_patches` (e.g. 576 patches for a 336×336 image)
- `n_q > 1` is always true

All three conditions are satisfied → `is_causal = 1` → the kernel masks out all key positions `k > query_pos` with `-INFINITY`. This converts ViT's **bidirectional** self-attention into **causal** (unidirectional) attention: patch 0 can only attend to itself, patch 575 is the only one with full context. Global semantic aggregation is destroyed across all full-attention layers (6 out of 28 layers in Qwen2.5-VL-3B), and the error compounds through every subsequent layer.

**Why LLM is unaffected:** In the flash attention kernel, `is_causal` and the explicit `mask` tensor are **two independent code paths**. llama.cpp's LLM prefill always constructs and passes an explicit lower-triangular causal mask tensor (`mask != NULL`), so it goes through the mask tensor path and never relies on `is_causal`. During decode, `n_q = 1` fails the `n_q > 1` check.

issues.title: Eval bug: Metal im2col pipeline/dispatch mismatch breaks 1D-conv audio encoders since b9433 (Qwen2-Audio outputs only "@@@@…")
issues.body_head:
### Name and Version

`b9433` (and every build after it). Last good build: `b9432`. macOS arm64, Apple Silicon.

### Operating systems

Mac

### GGML backends

Metal

### Hardware

Apple Silicon (reproduced on M-series).

### Models

`mradermacher/Qwen2-Audio-7B.Q8_0` (and corresponding mmproj). Any Whisper-style audio encoder is expected to be affected.

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

After upgrading from `b9432` → `b9433`, any prompt that includes an audio input produces a token loop, typically just `@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@…`. Text-only inference is unaffected. Image / vision inputs are also unaffected (verified with the same mmproj path on the latest build, `b9453`).

Minimal repro:

```bash
# works
./llama-mtmd-cli \
  -m  Qwen2-Audio-7B.Q8_0.gguf \
  --mmproj mmproj-Qwen2-Audio-7B.gguf \
  --audio samples/jfk.wav \
  -p "Please describe what you hear."
# build b9432  -> correct transcription
# build b9433+ -> "@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@…"
```

### First Bad Commit

`2d9b7c8` — PR #23901 "metal : restore im2col implementation for large kernels". It's the only commit between b9432 and b9433.

**Root cause**

The pipeline-selection criterion in `ggml_metal_library_get_pipeline_im2col` and the dispatch-selection criterion in `ggml_metal_op_im2col` disagree:

```cpp
// ggml/src/ggml-metal/ggml-metal-device.cpp – picks pipeline by src[0]->ne0 * ne1
if (ne00*ne01 <= 1024) base = "kernel_im2col_%s";
else                   base = "kernel_im2col_ext_%s";

// ggml/src/ggml-metal/ggml-metal-ops.cpp – picks dispatch by KH*KW
if (KH*KW <= max_threads_per_threadgroup(pipeline)) {
    // small-kernel dispatch: (IC, OH, OW) x (ntptg0, KH, KW)
} else {
    // large-kernel dispatch: (quotient*CHW, OH, OW) x (n_threads, 1, 1)
}
```

For 1D convolutions (`is_2D == false`) `KH = 1` and `KW = src[0]->ne[0]` (the kernel size). The Whisper-style audio encoder has kernel `[kw=3, in_channels=1280, …]`, so:

| Quantity        | Value             | Branch taken              |
| --------------- | ----------------- | ------------------------- |
| `ne00 * ne01`   | `3 * 1280 = 3840` | pipeline = `kernel_im2col_ext` |
| `KH * KW`       | `1 * 3 = 3`       | dispatch  = small-kernel  |

So the small-kernel dispatch geometry feeds the `_ext` kernel, which expects a completely different `tgpig/tgpg/tpitg/ntg` layout. The encoder writes garbage into the im2col output, the audio projector produces meaningless embeddings, and the LLM falls into a degenerate token loop (`@`).

F

Architecture: MoonViT-SO-400M (vision encoder, head_dim=72, 2D RoPE, 27-layer ViT) + Eagle MLP projector (2-layer MLP with intermediate LayerNorm) + Qwen2.5-3B Instruct (LLM backbone), with a 2×2 spatial patch merge between encoder and projector.

|---|---|
| llama.cpp commit | e4406fed5 (build 8540) |
| GPU | NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1050 Ti (4030 MiB, compute 6.1) |
| OS / Arch | Linux x86_64, GNU 11.4.0 |

  -m  ./LocateAnything-3B/LocateAnything-3B-LLM-Q4_K_M.gguf \
  --mmproj ./LocateAnything-3B/mmproj-LocateAnything-3B-BF16.gguf \
  --image ./Sample_dataset_312.jpg \

Actual output:

issues.title: Hexagon (HTP) backend: prefill produces garbage logits for ubatch ≥ 32 tokens (Qwen3, Hexagon v79)
issues.body_head:
### Summary

On the Hexagon NPU backend (`-DGGML_HEXAGON=ON`, `--device HTP0`), **prefill produces corrupted
logits when a ubatch contains ≥ 32 tokens** — generation is garbage from the very first sampled
token (e.g. `100 3 33 33 33 …`, mixed-script junk). With `--ubatch-size ≤ 16` the same prompt
produces correct, coherent output. The split logic is fine; the corruption is in the HTP compute
kernel's handling of the token (batch) dimension.

### Environment

- **Device:** OnePlus 13 — Snapdragon 8 Elite, **Hexagon arch v79** (`libggml-htp-v79.so`)
- **Backend:** `-DGGML_HEXAGON=ON -DGGML_OPENCL=ON`, built with the `snapdragon-toolchain`
  Docker image (`ghcr.io/snapdragon-toolchain/arm64-android:v0.7`, bundles Hexagon SDK 6.6 + NDK r28b)
- **llama.cpp:** tag `b9505` (commit `0066404`)
- **Model:** Qwen3.5-4B fine-tune, **Q4_0** (also reproduces on a 9B Q4_0)
- `GGML_HEXAGON_NDEV=1`, single HTP session

### Reproduction

```sh
# GARBAGE — first token onward is junk:
GGML_HEXAGON_NDEV=1 ./bin/llama-completion --device HTP0 -ngl 99 -m model-Q4_0.gguf \
  -p "The sun rose over the quiet valley. Birds sang in the tall pine trees. A farmer walked toward his field carrying a wooden bucket. The morning air was cool and smelled of grass. He paused to look at the distant mountains. Then he continued on his way." \
  -n 32 -c 4096 -ub 32 --temp 0

# COHERENT — same prompt, smaller ubatch:
... same command with -ub 16
```

Measured (binary-searched on a 150-token prompt): **ub ≤ 31 → coherent; ub = 32 → garbage.** The
break is **exactly at 32**, which equals one full HVX vector on v79 (1024-bit = 32 × fp32). A short
prompt (single ubatch < 32 tokens) is always correct, which is why trivial prompts appear to "work"
while any multi-sentence prompt corrupts.

### Likely cause (a lead, not a confirmed fix)

The corruption boundary lands exactly at **32 tokens along the batch dimension**, and HVX vectors on
Hexagon v79 are **1024 bits = 128 bytes = 32 × fp32**. This strongly suggests an **HVX
vectorization bug at the one-full-vector boundary** in the HTP matmul kernel (`ggml/src/ggml-hexagon/htp/`)
— correct for a partial vector (< 32 elements along the token axis), wrong once a full HVX vector (or
multiple vectors) is processed. `test-backend-ops -b HTP0 -o MUL_MAT` passes for tiny shapes (n ≤ 3),
which wouldn't exercise the ≥ 32 batch path.

### Workaround

Setting `n_ubatch = 31` (one element below the 32-element HVX boundary) gives correct output at some
prefill-throu

issues.title: [BUG] Qwen3.6-35B-A3B / llama-server merges consecutive images into 2 frames, causing incorrect image count and partial image understanding
issues.body_head:
## Summary

When using `llama-server` with `Qwen3.6-35B-A3B` and a matching `mmproj`, consecutive images in a single user message are sometimes merged into super-frames. As a result, 4 uploaded images are interpreted as 2 images, and the model can only describe part of the visual content.

## Environment

- `llama.cpp` release: `b9553`
- Model: `Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-Q4_K_M.gguf`
- mmproj: `mmproj-Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-BF16.gguf`
- Server: `llama-server`
- UI: browser chat page
- Also reproducible through the OpenAI-compatible API

## Reproduction steps

1. Start `llama-server` with:
   ```bash
   llama-server -m Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-Q4_K_M.gguf --mmproj mmproj-Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-BF16.gguf
   ```

2. Open the web UI.

3. Upload 4 images in one message.

4. Ask: `How many images are there?`

5. Observe that the model answers `2` instead of `4`.

## API reproduction

This works correctly if images are separated by text:

```json
{
  "messages": [
    {
      "role": "user",
      "content": [
        { "type": "text", "text": "[image 1]" },
        { "type": "image_url", "image_url": { "url": "<BASE64>" } },
        { "type": "text", "text": "[image 2]" },
        { "type": "image_url", "image_url": { "url": "<BASE64>" } },
        { "type": "text", "text": "[image 3]" },
        { "type": "image_url", "image_url": { "url": "<BASE64>" } },
        { "type": "text", "text": "[image 4]" },
        { "type": "image_url", "image_url": { "url": "<BASE64>" } },
        { "type": "text", "text": "How many images are there?" }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

In this case, the model answers `4`.

However, when the same 4 images are sent consecutively without text separators:

```json
{
  "messages": [
    {
      "role": "user",
      "content": [
        { "type": "image_url", "image_url": { "url": "<BASE64>" } },
        { "type": "image_url", "image_url": { "url": "<BASE64>" } },
        { "type": "image_url", "image_url": { "url": "<BASE64>" } },
        { "type": "image_url", "image_url": { "url": "<BASE64>" } },
        { "type": "text", "text": "How many images are there?" }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

the model answers `2`.

## Expected behavior

* All 4 images should be treated as 4 separate images.
* The model should answer `4`.
* The model should be able to describe content from all 4 images independently.

## Actual behavior

* Consecutive images appear to be merged into 2 units.
* The model answers `2`.
* When asked about the image contents, it only describes part of the images.

issues.title: Eval bug: HMX quantized matmul rework (#23368) produces repeated garbage tokens on HTP v81 (SM8845)
issues.body_head:
### Name and Version

Tested on commit `6ddc943` (which includes `c9872a2`)
Reverted to pre-`c9872a2` commit `9a532ae` as workaround.

### Operating systems

Android 12 (Qualcomm SM8845 / Snapdragon 8 Elite)

### GGML backends

Hexagon (HTP v81)

### Hardware

- SoC: Qualcomm SM8845 (Snapdragon 8 Elite)
- DSP: Hexagon HTP v81
- Device: DJI RC710
- Hexagon SDK: 6.4.0.2

### Models

- Qwen3-4B Q4_0
- Qwen3-4B Q8_0
- Qwen3.5-2B Q4_0
- Qwen3.5-2B Q8_0
- Gemma4-E2B Q4_0

All models reproduce the issue. **Not model-specific.**

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

After commit `c9872a2` (hexagon: HMX quantized matmul rework, PR #23368), all models produce repeated garbage tokens when running on Hexagon HTP v81.

**Symptoms:**
- Output consists of repeated tokens like `<unused17>`, `Us`, `Game`, `OF` etc.
- The same models work correctly on CPU
- The same models worked correctly on HTP v81 **before** `c9872a2`

**Key findings from investigation:**

1. **Not quantization-specific**: Both Q4_0 and Q8_0 produce the same garbage output. Tested with Qwen3.5-2B Q8_0 to rule out Q4 dequant issues — same result.

2. **Root cause is in `c9872a2`**: This commit rewrote the HMX matmul with two major changes:
   - Changed from **spatial mode** to **activation depth mode** (`HMX_SUPPORT_DEPTH`)
   - Rewrote dequant logic to use `HVX_vector_x2/4`
   - Removed non-pipelined matmul version

3. **Pre-`c9872a2` works perfectly**: On commit `9a532ae` (before the matmul rework), Qwen3-4B Q4_0 runs correctly on HTP v81 with 3 graph splits and correct output.

4. **Cannot revert**: 10+ subsequent hexagon commits depend on the new matmul interface (22 conflicts when attempting `git revert c9872a2`).

**Function signature change in skel:**

| Before (`9a532ae`) | After (`c9872a2`) |
|---|---|
| `hmx_mat_mul_permuted_w16a32` | `hmx_matmul_f16_f32` |
| `hmx_mat_mul_permuted_qk_0_d16a32` | `hmx_matmul_2d_f32` |
| | `hmx_matmul_id_2d_f32` |
| | `hmx_matmul_f16_f32_batched` |

**Steps to reproduce:**
1. Build llama.cpp at any commit after `c9872a2` with `GGML_HEXAGON=ON`
2. Run any Q4_0 or Q8_0 model on a device with HTP v81 (SM8845)
3. Observe repeated garbage token output

**Workaround:**
Use commit `9a532ae` or earlier (before `c9872a2`).

`c9872a2` — hexagon: HMX quantized matmul rework (#23368)

### Relevant log output

Output on HTP v81 after c9872a2 (garbage):

issues.title: Windows OpenVINO builds fail to start due to missing OpenSSL dependencies and incorrect release packaging
issues.body_head:
Windows OpenVINO builds (all recent versions) fail to start due to missing runtime dependencies and incorrect packaging structure.

### Issue 1: Missing OpenSSL dependencies + openvino.dll and tbb12.dll

When launching llama-server.exe (even with --help), the process fails immediately with:

- libcrypto-3-x64.dll not found
- libssl-3-x64.dll not found
- exit code: -1073741515 (0xC0000135)

No OpenSSL runtime DLLs are included in the release package.

Additional information:

After installing OpenSSL 3.x (Win64), the missing:

- libssl-3-x64.dll
- libcrypto-3-x64.dll

errors disappear.

However, llama-server.exe still fails to start because:

- openvino.dll not found
- tbb12.dll not found

So OpenSSL resolves only part of the dependency chain. This happens before any model is loaded and even when running:

llama-server.exe --help


### Issue 2: Incorrect directory structure on extraction

After extracting the release archive, files are placed into an unexpected structure:

C:\Users\...\versions\<build>\cpu\Release\llama-server.exe

Instead of a flat or standard layout like:

C:\Users\...\versions\<build>\cpu\llama-server.exe

Additionally, the LICENSE file is placed alongside the Release folder, but the actual binaries are nested inside the Release directory.

This differs from other backends (e.g. Vulkan), which do not use a nested Release folder.

### Environment
- Windows 10/11
- llama.cpp OpenVINO Windows builds (latest CI artifacts)
- Extracted from official release archive

### Expected behavior
- All required runtime DLLs should be included OR clearly documented as external dependencies
- Release archive should have consistent and flat structure across backends
- Executable should run immediately after extraction (or clear setup instructions provided)

### Actual behavior
- Missing libssl-3-x64.dll and libcrypto-3-x64.dll, openvino.dll and tbb12.dll
- Executable fails before initialization
- Inconsistent folder structure (Release subdirectory only for OpenVINO builds)

issues.title: metal: rope_back operator (#24725) causes generation quality regression on Gemma 4 26B A4B (Apple Silicon)
issues.body_head:
## Summary

Commit 0843245cb (`metal: implement rope_back operator, #24725`) causes a significant
generation quality regression for Gemma 4 26B A4B on Apple Silicon (Metal). Found while
running a local inference benchmark suite. Agentic task success rate drops from 100%
to 66.7% across two independent runs.

## Platform

- Apple M3 Max 64GB, macOS 15
- Metal backend (`-ngl 999 -fa on`)
- Model: `gemma-4-26B-A4B-it-qat` (Q4_K_XL GGUF), MTP draft head enabled (`--spec-type draft-mtp`)

## Bisect

| build | commit | SR | notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| b9620 | 57fe1f07c | 100% | 3 runs, all clean |
| b9689 | 8d2e58063 | **100%** | post bf16-concat (#24724), **pre rope_back** |
| b9692 | f3e182816 | **66.7%** | post rope_back — 2/2 runs regressed |

b9689 (post #24724, pre #24725) is fully clean. Adding rope_back alone causes the regression.

## Symptoms

- Task success rate 100% → 66.7% on agentic coding benchmarks (multi-turn, tool-calling)
- One run produced a 620s generation on a task that normally takes 90–175s (model entered
  a generation loop)
- Failures are stochastic across different tasks (not always the same task), suggesting
  general generation quality degradation rather than a specific broken path
- Qwen3.6-35B-A3B tests are unaffected (±1% on b9692)

## Notes

rope_back is a training-time operator (backward pass for RoPE). It's unclear why its
Metal implementation would affect forward-pass inference, but the bisect is unambiguous.
Possibly the Metal kernel shares state or buffers with the forward rope kernel in a way
that causes interference at inference time.

The most reproducible symptom is an assistant response consisting almost entirely of repeated `?` characters, while the HTTP/SSE stream remains structurally valid and `curl` exits successfully.

I am on 9682 (558e221b7).

This looks possibly related to #20610 and #21888, but my case is not identical:

I have seen some very promising results with the hardware when the responses are healthy, the generation is fast, the GPUs are great value and you can fit so many models on it. If we could solve this issue, that would make AI accessible to a whole generation of cards.

Note that in this ticket, I refer and test a lot Qwen but I had a similar experience with Gemma4 producing '<unused49>' tokens. Disabling the reasoning stabilized the model but after that it was unable to perform in agentic scenarios (it basically tell you it will do something and never does it). issues.title: Misc. bug: ROCm backend reports incorrect free VRAM
issues.body_head:
### Name and Version

version: 9759 (099b579ac)
built with GNU 16.1.1 for Linux x86_64

### Operating systems

Linux

### Which llama.cpp modules do you know to be affected?

libllama (core library)

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

`hipMemGetInfo` on AMD with ROCm reports nearly all VRAM as free regardless of actual usage by other processes. The Vulkan backend reports correct values.

`hipMemGetInfo` queries `HSA_AMD_AGENT_INFO_MEMORY_AVAIL`, which bottoms out at the KFD kernel ioctl `AMDKFD_IOC_AVAILABLE_MEMORY`, handled by `amdgpu_amdkfd_get_available_memory()`. It does not subtract for any DRM graphics allocations (Vulkan, OpenGL, compositor). It only accounts for VRAM allocated through KFD itself (ROCm compute) and all pinned BOs (display scanout, firmware...). Thus, `hipMemGetInfo` is blind to any VRAM not allocated via the ROCm stack.

Notably, AMD's own ROCm SMI library reads `mem_info_vram_used` from sysfs as its primary memory query path, with the KFD ioctl only as a fallback, so I'm not sure if it's on purpose or not that `hipMemGetInfo` do not report the true available VRAM.

I would also like to know what `cudaMemGetInfo` is reporting (don't have a CUDA setup to test), is it also only accounting for VRAM used allocated through it or is it accounting for VRAM used for compositor or a game? If it's the latter then I should also report it upstream as HIP is supposed to mimic CUDA, and it could easily be an oversight from using GPUs on server only for compute.

Here is a simple example from my desktop:

### Idle

| Source                  |    Total |     Free |    Used |
| ----------------------- | -------- | -------- | ------- |
| `hipMemGetInfo()`       | 16384 MiB | 16334 MiB | 50 MiB  |
| sysfs (`mem_info_vram`) | 16384 MiB | 14904 MiB | 1480 MiB |

### With a video game running

| Source                  |    Total |     Free |    Used |
| ----------------------- | -------- | -------- | ------- |
| `hipMemGetInfo()`       | 16384 MiB | 16326 MiB | 58 MiB  |
| sysfs (`mem_info_vram`) | 16384 MiB | 11449 MiB | 4935 MiB |

issues.title: Misc. bug: ggml Vulkan op_step vs CPU ggml_step mismatch at x==0
issues.body_head:
### Name and Version

version: 9204 (726704a16)
built with GNU 11.5.0 for Linux x86_64

### Operating systems

Linux

### Which llama.cpp modules do you know to be affected?

libllama (core library)

### Command line

```shell

```

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

First: I know this is against an older build, but I have verified that the core issue remains in master - though the specific placement of the code has changed a little (the Vulkan code is the standalone step.comp, same >=. It was merged into unary.comp since; the >= survived the refactor).

Anyhow, while chasing performance gains on my Strix box I noticed that ggml's step unary op returns a different value at x == 0 on CPU vs the Vulkan backend. 

_For CPU (reference)_: 
ggml/src/ggml-cpu/vec.h ~L903 `ggml_vec_step_f32 y[i] = (x[i] > 0.f) ? 1.f : 0.f; -> step(0) = 0`


_For Vulkan_: 
ggml/src/ggml-vulkan/vulkan-shaders/unary.comp ~L45 `op_step return x >= 0.0f ? 1.0f : 0.0f; -> step(0) = 1`

It might be worth checking Metal / CUDA / SYCL / OpenCL step for the same >= vs > - I have not.


Why does this matter?  The step op will give a different result on CPU (step(0)=0) vs Vulkan (step(0)=1), so any graph relying on the standard step(0)=0 will give wrong results on Vulkan while matching CPU.


Repro:
Runnable (any machine with a Vulkan device):
```
cmake -B build -DGGML_VULKAN=ON && cmake --build build --target test-backend-ops
# Stock STEP test PASSES — it never sees x==0 (input is random uniform [-150, 150]):
./build/bin/test-backend-ops -o STEP

# Force a zero input to expose it. In tests/test-backend-ops.cpp,
# test_unary::initialize_tensors(), right before the init_tensor_uniform loop, add:
#     if (op == GGML_UNARY_OP_STEP) { min = 0.f; max = 0.f; }
# rebuild, rerun:
./build/bin/test-backend-ops -o STEP
# -> STEP now FAILS on Vulkan:  [STEP] ERR = 1.000000000   (CPU step(0)=0 vs Vulkan step(0)=1)
```

issues.title: DeepSeek-V4: quantized K-cache (--cache-type-k q8_0) produces garbage on all backends — attention rotation forces the model off its sparse attention paths
issues.body_head:
## Summary

DeepSeek-V4(-Flash) with a quantized K-cache (`--cache-type-k q8_0`) produces confident gibberish on **every backend** (CPU and CUDA verified identically) while the server stays healthy — no error, no abort. With `--cache-type-k f16` output is correct. Root-caused to the attention-rotation (Hadamard incoherence) path forcing the model off its sparse attention implementation.

## Minimal reproduction

Any DeepSeek-V4-Flash GGUF (tested: two independently sha256-verified unsloth quants, `UD-Q4_K_XL` and `Q4_K_M-XL`):

```
llama-server -m DeepSeek-V4-Flash-UD-Q4_K_XL-00001-of-00005.gguf -fa on --cache-type-k q8_0 --cache-type-v q8_0
# CPU-only (-ngl 0) is sufficient to reproduce
curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8080/completion -d '{"prompt":"The capital of France is","n_predict":12,"temperature":0}'
```

Result: `" newcom wrt wrtêu newcom dialog大有lean…"` (identical signature on CPU and 8× V100 CUDA).
With `--cache-type-k f16` (V may stay q8_0): `" Paris."` — correct.

## Root cause

1. A quantized K/V cache enables the Hadamard incoherence rotation (`attn_rot_k`/`attn_rot_v`), allocating `self_k_rot`.
2. DeepSeek-V4's attention dispatch (`models/deepseek4.cpp`, `build_attention`) requires `self_k_rot == nullptr` to take its designed sparse CSA/HCA/lightning-indexer paths; a non-null `self_k_rot` **diverts every affected layer to `build_raw_attention`**.
3. `build_raw_attention` applies the rotation with a plain `ggml_mul_mat` instead of the block-reshaping `ggml_mul_mat_aux` the standard path uses, **and** never un-rotates the MLA V-is-a-view-of-K output before the `v_mla` up-projection (compare `build_attn`'s `cur = ggml_mul_mat_aux(cur, v_rot)`).

Graph-level, therefore backend-independent — which matches the identical CPU/CUDA corruption. f16-K never enables the rotation, hence unaffected.

## Isolation proof (the kernels are fine)

`test-backend-ops` cases added at hsk=576/hsv=512 (V as a sub-view of K) with q8_0: FLASH_ATTN_EXT 56/56 PASS and SET_ROWS (quantize-on-write) 2/2 PASS, CUDA-vs-CPU — the FA read kernels and the K-cache write kernel are numerically correct in isolation. The defect is purely the rotation path composition in the live graph.

Additional discriminator: disabling all rotations at runtime (patch adding an env override, incl. the forced-indexer rotation) with q8_0 K/V → coherent on CPU.

## Live verification of the minimal fix

Disabling the KV Hadamard rotation for `LLM_ARCH_DEEPSEEK4` (so quantized K flows through the model's de

issues.title: SYCL: MUL_MAT_ID prefill path produces wrong results on Intel Arc Pro B70 (Battlemage G31) — causes garbage output on MoE models
issues.body_head:
### Description

`test-backend-ops -b SYCL0 -o MUL_MAT_ID` fails 28/792 cases on Intel Arc Pro B70 (Battlemage G31), all in the non-decode (prefill/batched, `ne12 > 1`) path of `ggml_sycl_mul_mat_id()`. Errors are large numerical mismatches (0.3–1.9, tolerance is 0.0005), not close-call rounding.

I originally hit this while debugging garbage/gibberish output from a real MoE model (Qwen3.6-35B-A3B) running on the SYCL backend — the same model on the Vulkan backend of the same GPU produces fully correct, coherent output at similar speed, so the corruption is SYCL-specific.

### Investigation so far

- Confirmed **not** related to any of `GGML_SYCL_ENABLE_OPT`, `GGML_SYCL_ENABLE_VMM`, `GGML_SYCL_ENABLE_FUSION`, `GGML_SYCL_USE_ASYNC_MEM_OP` — disabling each individually (and all together) does not change the failure set.
- Suspected the counting-sort refactor from #23142 (`mmid_counting_sort_rows` / current `k_copy_src1_to_contiguous`) — tested by temporarily reverting `ggml_sycl_mul_mat_id()`'s `ne12 > 1` branch to the pre-#23142 atomic-scan implementation (old `k_copy_src1_to_contiguous`/`k_copy_dst_from_contiguous` with `dev_cur_src1_row` atomic counter). **Same failure set reproduces**, and in fact gets *worse* — several cases that were "just" large numerical errors under the new code produce outright `NaN`/`inf` under the old code. This points to a bug in a lower-level shared path (e.g. `ggml_sycl_op_mul_mat`/`ggml_sycl_op_mul_mat_sycl` when fed the row-gathered/contiguous tensor shapes used by `mul_mat_id`), not in the #23142 refactor itself.
- Already has #24676 (use-after-free fix) and #24452 (reordered Q4_K/Q5_K/Q6_K MoE support) merged — neither affects this.
- Decode path (`ne12 == 1`, `ggml_sycl_mul_mat_id_mmvq_fused`) is unaffected — only the prefill/batched path with more than one token per sequence.

The CPU backend can silently produce an incorrect result. 2. The CUDA backend may report that the operation is supported, but the selected kernel later triggers an assertion. 3. An existing backend test case is not executed by any backend under test, which hides both problems. ### 1. issues.body_head:
### Name and Version

llama-server, version b9940 (259f2e2a5), built with Clang 20.1.8 for Windows
x86_64, CUDA backend (cublas64_13 / CUDA 13.3 runtime).

### Operating systems

Windows

### GGML backends

CUDA

### Hardware

Windows 10 Enterprise 10.0.19045; 2× RTX 3090 (24 GB each); 128 GB RAM.

### Models

UD-Q3_K_XL (~120 GB, 4-way split GGUF) 
UD-IQ1_S (~77 GB, 3-way split)

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

### What happened?

With DeepSeek-V4-Flash GGUF models, output quality degrades in direct proportion
to how many MoE expert layers are computed on CUDA GPUs. With all experts kept
on CPU (`--n-cpu-moe 999`), output is fully coherent. As `--n-cpu-moe` is
lowered (more expert layers on GPU), the model progressively degrades: it
starts answering in the wrong language (Latvian instead of the requested
Lithuanian — i.e. "almost right" tokens) and becomes increasingly incoherent.

| --n-cpu-moe (model has 43 layers) | expert layers on GPU | output |
|---|---|---|
| 64 / 999 (all experts on CPU) | 0 | correct: coherent Lithuanian, can write a poem |
| 34 | 9 | wrong language (Latvian), degraded coherence |
| 30–32 | 11–13 | worse: barely coherent, cannot complete simple creative tasks |

Key facts:
- Reproduces identically on **two different quants**: UD-Q3_K_XL (~120 GB, 4-way
  split GGUF) and UD-IQ1_S (~77 GB, 3-way split) from
  https://huggingface.co/unsloth/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-GGUF — so it is not a
  quant-specific artifact.
- Expert tensor **placement should be mathematically neutral**; only this arch
  misbehaves. On the same machine/build, `gemma4` and `qwen35moe` MoE models
  run fully GPU-offloaded with correct output, so the CUDA setup itself is fine.
- Non-expert weights (attention etc.) on GPU are fine: runs with attention on
  GPU + all experts on CPU produce correct output.
- Not the known CUDA 13.2 gibberish issue — this build links `cublas64_13.dll`
  (CUDA runtime 13.3).

1. Load DeepSeek-V4-Flash UD-Q3_K_XL (or UD-IQ1_S):

3. Observe wrong-language / incoherent output.
4. Relaunch with `--n-cpu-moe 999` (all experts on CPU), same prompt →

issues.title: Eval bug: SM_60 Quality Loss, FP32 math silently done in FP16, fix merged in two forks.
issues.body_head:
### Name and Version

version: 9967 (4f37f5197)

### Operating systems

Linux

### GGML backends

CUDA

### Hardware

Linux / CUDA / 4× Tesla P100-PCIE-16GB (sm_60), dual Xeon, driver 580.159.03, CUDA 12.4. Tested on Ubuntu Server 26.04.

### Models

Qwen3.6-27B Q6_K (22,523,238,624 bytes) for the quality panel; Qwen3.6-4B dense and Darwin-36B-A3B (Qwen3.5-MoE arch) Q6_K for the speed legs.

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

SM_60 currently gets put into a hardware accelerated fast-path by default, which uses a FP16 hardware accelerator. The problem is that some FP32 math is silently getting truncated to FP16 that shouldn't be, causing significant accuracy deviations from baseline (0.002298 median KL divergence vs FP32 reference/1-in-29 flipped top tokens).

The fix for this is to carve out SM_60 the same way SM_61 already is, bypassing the Fast Path gate, and keeping FP32 math at 32 bits as it should be.

## How to Fix

261- #if defined(FP16_AVAILABLE) && __CUDA_ARCH__ != 610
261+ #if defined(FP16_AVAILABLE) && __CUDA_ARCH__ != 610 && __CUDA_ARCH__ != 600

305-        (GGML_CUDA_CC_IS_NVIDIA(cc) && fp16_available(cc) && ggml_cuda_highest_compiled_arch(cc) != 610) ||
305+        (GGML_CUDA_CC_IS_NVIDIA(cc) && fp16_available(cc) && ggml_cuda_highest_compiled_arch(cc) != 610 && ggml_cuda_highest_compiled_arch(cc) != 600) ||

311-    return (GGML_CUDA_CC_IS_NVIDIA(cc) && cc >= GGML_CUDA_CC_PASCAL && cc != 610) || GGML_CUDA_CC_IS_AMD(cc) ||
311+    return (GGML_CUDA_CC_IS_NVIDIA(cc) && cc >= GGML_CUDA_CC_PASCAL && cc != 610 && cc != 600) || GGML_CUDA_CC_IS_AMD(cc) ||

TheTom (Tom Turney) has shipped: https://github.com/TheTom/llama-cpp-turboquant/releases/tag/tqp-v0.3.0 
https://github.com/TheTom/llama-cpp-turboquant/pull/212 
spiritbuun has merged: https://github.com/spiritbuun/buun-llama-cpp/pull/80

1. Build stock llama.cpp using  `-DCMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES=60`.
2. Generate the truth base, run `llama-perplexity --kl-divergence-base out.kld` with fp32 KV, FA off,

3. Compare the stock vs patched runs against that base with `--kl-divergence`, 2048 ctx, 32 chunks.

issues.title: Eval bug: hy_v3 loads exp_probs_b with no .bias suffix — existing Hy3 GGUFs (AngelSlim, pre-merge quants) fail with "wrong number of tensors; expected 1298, got 1218"
issues.body_head:
### Name and Version

llama-server, build b10000 (also reproduced reading the source at tag b10000). Built from `.devops/cuda.Dockerfile` (CUDA 12.8.1), Linux x86_64, 2×P5000.

### Operating systems

Linux

### Which llama.cpp modules do you know to be affected?

libllama (core library)

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

The merged hy_v3 support (#25395) loads the MoE expert-selection bias with a **bare** tensor name:

```cpp
// src/models/hy-v3.cpp
layer.ffn_exp_probs_b = create_tensor(tn(LLM_TENSOR_FFN_EXP_PROBS_B,           i), {n_expert}, TENSOR_NOT_REQUIRED);
```

i.e. `blk.N.exp_probs_b`, while **every other MoE arch** in the tree loads it as `blk.N.exp_probs_b.bias`:

```
src/models/deepseek2.cpp:  tn(LLM_TENSOR_FFN_EXP_PROBS_B, "bias", i)
src/models/afmoe.cpp:      tn(LLM_TENSOR_FFN_EXP_PROBS_B, "bias", i)
src/models/lfm2moe.cpp:    tn(LLM_TENSOR_FFN_EXP_PROBS_B, "bias", i)
src/models/dots1.cpp:      tn(LLM_TENSOR_FFN_EXP_PROBS_B, "bias", i)   (etc.)
```

The bare name is consistent with what the b10000 converter emits for hy_v3 (the HF tensor is `model.layers.N.mlp.expert_bias`, which maps by exact match, so no `.bias` suffix is carried over) — but it is **incompatible with every existing public Hy3 GGUF**, because those were all produced with the pre-merge patch stacks, which named the tensor `blk.N.exp_probs_b.bias` (matching the convention of all other MoE arches):

* **AngelSlim/Hy3-GGUF** (Tencent's own quantization team; `Hy3-IQ1_M-mtp.gguf`, `Hy3-Q4_K_M-mtp.gguf`, …) — built with the patch stack shipped in that repo (`patches/01-hyv3-arch.patch` uses `tn(LLM_TENSOR_FFN_EXP_PROBS_B, "bias", i)`).

Loading any of these on b10000 fails with:

```
llama_model_load: error loading model: done_getting_tensors: wrong number of tensors; expected 1298, got 1218
```

(80 = one `exp_probs_b.bias` per MoE layer, 79 trunk + 1 NextN/MTP layer, none of them consumed.)

**Repro:**

```
llama-server -m Hy3-IQ1_M-mtp.gguf   # any AngelSlim/Hy3-GGUF file, b10000
```

### Suggested fix

Accept both spellings (verified working locally against both GGUF generations — AngelSlim `.bias` files and PR #25364-era bare-name files):

```cpp
layer.ffn_exp_probs_b = create_tensor(tn(LLM_TENSOR_FFN_EXP_PROBS_B, "bias",   i), {n_expert}, TENSOR_NOT_REQUIRED);
if (!layer.ffn_exp_probs_b) {
    layer.ffn_exp_probs_b = create_tensor(tn(LLM_TENSOR_FFN_EXP_PROBS_B,           i), {n_expert}, TENSOR_NOT_REQUIRED);
}
```

Alternatively, standardize the hy_v3 converter o

issues.title: Vulkan: wrong matmul results on Adreno (subgroupSize=128) — warptile WM exceeds BM (implicit `WM <= BM` invariant violated for subgroupSize > 64)
issues.body_head:
## Environment
- llama.cpp commit `bf2c86d` (also present in whisper.cpp's bundled ggml — its own tree must be patched too)
- Vulkan backend, **Adreno 650** via Mesa Turnip, `subgroupSize = 128` (double threadsize)
- Applies to **any device that reports `subgroupSize > 64`**, not just Adreno

## Symptom
`./test-backend-ops -b Vulkan0 -o MUL_MAT` — **2 of 229 f16 cases FAIL** with large error,
all of them **batched + broadcast + partial-tile** shapes:
```
MUL_MAT(type_a=f16,type_b=f32,m=64, n=45,k=128,bs=[8,1],nr=[4,1])  ERR = 0.414  FAIL
MUL_MAT(type_a=f16,type_b=f32,m=128,n=45,k=64, bs=[8,1],nr=[4,1])  ERR = 1.079  FAIL
```
Real workloads (whisper.cpp) produce **garbage / looping output** on the GPU while the
CPU backend on the same model is correct.

## Root cause
In `ggml_vk_load_shaders()` (`ggml/src/ggml-vulkan/ggml-vulkan.cpp`), warptiles are built
with **WM** (index 4) and **WARP** (index 10) = `subgroup_size_8 = max(device->subgroup_size, 8)`:
```cpp
l_warptile = { 128, 128, 128, 16, subgroup_size_8 * 2, 64, 2, ..., subgroup_size_8 }; // BM=128, WM=subgroup*2
m_warptile = { 128,  64,  64, 16, subgroup_size_8,     32, 2, ..., subgroup_size_8 }; // BM=64,  WM=subgroup
```
These encode an implicit invariant **`WM <= BM`**. It holds for
`subgroupSize ∈ {8,16,32,64}` but **breaks at 128**: `m_warptile` gets `WM = 128 > BM = 64`,
`l_warptile` gets `WM = 256 > BM = 128`.

In `mul_mm.comp` this detonates in three ways for the degenerate tile:
1. `BM / WM` folds to **0** (unsigned) → `warp_r = warp_i % (BM/WM)` / `warp_c = warp_i / (BM/WM)` are `udiv`/`umod` by zero.
2. `buf_a` shared-memory indexing addresses rows `0..WM-1`, but `buf_a` is only
   `BM * SHMEM_STRIDE` entries; for `WM > BM` it **runs past its end into `buf_b`**, so the
   `A` operands become `B` data.
3. Only the first `WN` of the `BN` output columns are ever written; columns `WN..BN-1` are
   **never computed/stored**.

The **small tile** (`s_warptile`) uses `BM = WM = subgroup_size_32` so it stays
self-consistent — which is exactly why **only medium/large tiles fail** (need `n > 32`
*and* `m > 32`); every *passing* case in the suite is a small-tile case.

## Fix (verified working)
Clamp the tiling WARP for the `l_`/`m_` warptiles to 64, **leaving `s_warptile` untouched**:
```cpp
const uint32_t subgroup_size_8 = std::max(device->subgroup_size, 8u);
const uint32_t mm_warp_8       = std::min(subgroup_size_8, 64u);           // NEW: l_/m_ warptiles only
const uint32_t mul_mat_mm_warp_8 = std:

issues.title: Metal: MTLDispatchTypeConcurrent dependency-tracking race on GCN/Vega (wave64) discrete GPUs — corrupted output and hard command-buffer failures
issues.body_head:
Related: #19431 (FA perf gap, non-Apple-Silicon Metal) and #19563 (garbled output on Radeon Pro 5300M) — same neighborhood (non-Apple-Silicon Metal correctness/perf gaps) but a distinct root cause from either.

**Hardware:** AMD Radeon VII (GCN, discrete, `threadExecutionWidth` probes at 64) via Metal backend on an Intel Mac (no unified memory).

**Context:** While adding a 64-wide-SIMD ("wave64") decode path to get GPU-resident mat-vec ops working on this hardware class (Apple Silicon and AMD RDNA report 32; GCN/Vega report 64, breaking the 32-wide assumption baked into the existing Metal kernels), we hit output corruption that traced to the scheduler, not the kernels:

- Confirmed not a per-op kernel bug: dispatch-skip bisection on a 12B model exonerated every individual kernel one at a time — output stayed corrupted with the SOFT_MAX kernel body gutted and with entire op families' dispatches skipped.
- The scheduler's `MTLDispatchTypeConcurrent`-based dependency tracking (used so independent ops can overlap in a command buffer) hadn't been exercised against the much higher density of GPU-resident mat-vec ops that a full wave64 decode step puts on the graph. Toggling `GGML_METAL_CONCURRENCY_DISABLE=1` reliably flips the corruption off, confirming a scheduling race, not a compute error.
- Splitting the *same* dispatch stream across more command buffers eliminates it; splitting at the encoder level inside one command buffer does not — only command-buffer granularity avoids the race.

**Fix applied (local fork, not yet a clean upstream PR):** force serial dispatch specifically when a wave64-class device is decoding — `use_concurrency = ctx->use_concurrency && !wave64_decode` — leaving normal wave32/RDNA and wave64 *prefill* on full concurrent dispatch. No perf regression measured on the affected 8B/12B models (24-25 t/s decode, matching non-wave64-class cards at equivalent size).

**Separately, and worth flagging even though it's outside the wave64 patch's scope:** with the fix's env flag *off* (i.e. exercising `MTLDispatchTypeConcurrent`'s stock/default path on this same GCN/Vega hardware, no wave64-specific code involved), we could reliably reproduce a hard failure — not just corrupted output — on 6/6 attempts, fresh server each run, identical signature every time: `ggml_metal_synchronize: error: command buffer 0 failed with status 5` → `llama_decode: failed to decode, ret = -3`. server: inconsistent `created` timestamp in `/v1/models` endpoint breaks client caching
issues.body_head:
## Summary

The `created` field in the `/v1/models` endpoint response is regenerated as the current Unix timestamp on every request (or at least on every server restart), rather than being set once at server startup or model load time.

This behavior differs from other OpenAI-compatible inference servers (e.g., vLLM, Ollama) and breaks client-side caching mechanisms that rely on deterministic responses.

## Current Behavior

The `created` field contains a dynamic Unix timestamp that changes between requests:

**Request 1:**
```json
{
  "data": [{
    "id": "model-name",
    "object": "model",
    "created": 1785134428,
    "owned_by": "llamacpp"
  }]
}
```

**Request 2 (after some time):**
```json
{
  "data": [{
    "id": "model-name",
    "object": "model",
    "created": 1785136128,
    "owned_by": "llamacpp"
  }]
}
```

## Expected Behavior

The `created` field should be set once (e.g., at server startup or model load time) and remain constant across requests. This aligns with how other inference servers handle this field and with the OpenAI API convention where `created` represents when the resource was instantiated in the service.

## Impact

This causes issues for clients that implement caching based on the `/v1/models` response payload. Every request to the endpoint results in a cache miss due to the changing timestamp, leading to unnecessary network calls and preventing efficient idle/sleep management in proxy servers.

## Proposed Fix

Store the timestamp once at server initialization (e.g., using a static variable set at `main()` startup) rather than calling `time(0)` / `time(nullptr)` on each request.

## References

- OpenAI API Models object documentation defines `created` as: "The Unix timestamp (in seconds) when the model was created."
- Other inference servers (vLLM, Ollama) set this field once at startup.
- llama.cpp server README documents the endpoint but does not specify the dynamic nature of this field.

---

**Note:** I am aware this is a minor change. However, it improves compatibility with clients relying on deterministic API responses for caching purposes. I'm happy to implement a PR for this if the maintainers are open to the change.

issues.title: server: prompt cache is reused across requests with different per-request `lora` — output silently contaminated by the previous adapter
issues.body_head:
### Summary

With adapters loaded via `--lora ... --lora-init-without-apply` and selected
per-request via the `lora: [{id, scale}]` field, the server reuses cached prompt
KV across requests that select **different** adapters. KV computed while adapter
A was active is reused for a request selecting adapter B whenever the prompt
prefix matches. The request succeeds, nothing is logged, and the output is
partially influenced by the wrong adapter.

This bites any multi-adapter server whose requests share prompt prefixes (our
case: several persona adapters over one base, common system prefix). The
workaround is `cache_prompt: false` on every request, which works but costs the
full prompt re-processing on every call.

### Reproduction (b10121, server-cuda)

1. `llama-server -m base.gguf --lora A.gguf --lora B.gguf
   --lora-init-without-apply -np 1` — any two adapters with visibly different
   effects.
2. Request 1: long prompt P, `"lora": [{"id": 0, "scale": 1.0}]`,
   `"cache_prompt": true`.
3. Request 2: same prompt P, `"lora": [{"id": 1, "scale": 1.0}]`,
   `"cache_prompt": true`.
4. Request 2's `timings.prompt_n` shows the prefix was not re-evaluated, and its
   output differs from the same request run on a cold slot.

### Suggested fix

Treat a change in the resolved per-request lora config like a prompt mismatch:
invalidate the slot's cached prefix (or key the cache on the lora config). An
opt-in flag would already let multi-adapter servers cache safely.

### Related, secondary observation

With `--jinja` on the same build, the jinja-derived output parser returns HTTP
500 when the model produces degenerate text that never matches the expected
structure — similar territory to #20729 / #20260 / #21771. `--no-jinja` avoids
it. Mentioning it here for context; happy to file separately if useful.

issues.body_head:
## Describe the bug

Commit `caa596ab3` disables MMQ on devices with less than 48 KiB per-block shared memory. On RTX 3090 (compute capability 8.6, Ampere), this incorrectly disables MMQ, causing prefill to fall back to a much slower path.

## Expected behavior

MMQ should remain enabled on RTX 3090 since it has sufficient shared memory (48 KiB per block).

## Actual behavior

After commit caa596ab3:
- Prefill (PP) drops from ~1200 t/s to ~40 t/s (CPU-level performance)
- Token generation (TG) is unaffected
- GPU utilization drops to ~0% during prefill
- Reverting the commit restores normal performance (~100+ t/s with GPU util ~46%)

## Steps to reproduce

1. Use RTX 3090 (or any Ampere GPU with exactly 48 KiB shared memory per block)
2. Build llama.cpp at commit caa596ab3 with `-DLLAMA_CUDA=ON`
3. Run a large prompt (>4K tokens) with `-ngl 99`
4. Observe prefill speed (~40 t/s) and GPU utilization (~0%)

## Additional context

The check at `ggml/src/ggml-cuda/mmq.cu:302`:
```cpp
if (smpbo < 48 * 1024) {
    return false;
}
```

On RTX 3090, `smpbo` returns exactly 48 KiB (49152 bytes), and the strict less-than comparison should pass. However, the device appears to report a value that triggers this guard. This may also affect other Ampere GPUs.

**Workaround:** Revert commit caa596ab3 locally.

## Environment

- GPU: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3090 (24GB)
- Driver: 580.173.02 (CUDA 13.0)
- llama.cpp: master @ caa596ab3
- Model: Qwen3.6-27B (IQ4_XS, MTP variant)
- OS: Ubuntu 26.04
